what: Satellite pre-check of ZARC-NM indicators 4 (years without soil disturbance) and 5 (straw cover in pre-sowing) for three 9 ha cropland quadrats of Cruz Alta (RS), 1984-2026, applying IN SPA/MAPA 2/2025 items 6.2-6.8 and Table 1 where the norm gives definitions or thresholds.
norm: Instrucao Normativa SPA/MAPA n. 2/2025 (ZARC Niveis de Manejo), items 2 (Table 1), 3.2.1, 6.2-6.8

applied_from_norm.quadrat_size: 9 ha (300 m x 300 m); norm item 6.2 IV: 5-10 ha for fields > 100 ha
applied_from_norm.sensors: Landsat C2 L2 (TM, ETM+, OLI, OLI-2) and HLS v2.0 L30 at 30 m (item 6.4; S30 left out, plan_b)
applied_from_norm.all_images: every scene of WRS-2 223/080, 222/080 and HLS L30 tiles T22JBP/T22JBN, 15 Sep - 31 Dec, with >= 80 of the 100 quadrat pixels clear (item 6.5 asks for all images, >= every 16 days)

chosen_here_not_in_norm.pre_sowing_month: the norm uses the month before sowing (item 6.7); the sowing date is not known, so the reference is the clear observation with the lowest mean NDTI among no-green observations of 15 Sep - 31 Dec (minNDTI, Zheng et al. 2012), or the seasonal NDVI minimum if the quadrat was never without green
chosen_here_not_in_norm.c_embrapa: residue cover C of the no-green pixels (NDVI < 0.30; Doc 454 masks NDVI > 0.3) on the reference date, from the Embrapa Documentos 454 ruler: quadratic fitted to its Table 2 (19 fields, Cambe PR, Sentinel-2, transect); the norm itself gives no NDTI-to-cover conversion. C >= 80% is reported as level '3 or 4' because the document states NDTI saturates near 80% cover. Calibrated on another soil, region and sensor: not validated in Cruz Alta
chosen_here_not_in_norm.tillage_signal: at least one clear observation with >= 50% of the quadrat pixels at C < 30% by the Embrapa ruler (ploughed fields in Doc 454 Table 2 had 5-20% cover). The team threshold (NDVI < 0.30 and NDTI < 0.06) is kept as team_threshold_* for comparison
chosen_here_not_in_norm.years_since_last_signal: years since the last season with a bare-soil signature; a season with fewer than 3 clear observations (or none) cannot exclude a tillage, so T then restarts as a lower bound (years_since_is_lower_bound true; the indicator-4 level is then 'at least N'). A season that stays green in >= 3 clear observations counts as watched without a signature

embrapa_ruler.source: Embrapa Soja, Documentos 454 (2023), Table 2 (19 fields, Cambe PR, Sentinel-2 29/10/2021, transect cover), quadratic fitted here; saturation near 80% stated on p. 29
embrapa_ruler.equation: C = -10275.5 * NDTI^2 + 2265.4 * NDTI + -27.76, flat at 97.1% above NDTI 0.110, clipped to 0-100
embrapa_ruler.conditions: north Parana (Cambe), clayey Latossolo, corn and wheat residue, Sentinel-2, one date; not Cruz Alta, not Landsat TM/ETM+/OLI, not HLS: transferred without local calibration

quadrat_rule: 300 m blocks on the UTM 22S 30 m grid entirely ESA WorldCover 2021 cropland inside the municipality and clear on both before/after map dates (1991-11-04 and 2026-10-20); one per NASADEM slope class (< 3%, 3-8%, >= 8% block mean), closest to the class median slope, >= 5 km apart. No property, owner or registry (CAR) was looked up; the quadrats are not real field samples.
plan_b: HLS S30 (the Sentinel-2 half of HLS) was left out for time; Landsat 4-9 and HLS L30 give every year 1984-2026 (16-day revisit per Landsat, 8 days with two in orbit). Reading S30 would add observations only from 2020 on.
caveats: No field calibration in Cruz Alta: the Embrapa ruler was calibrated in Cambe (PR) on 19 fields with Sentinel-2; Cruz Alta straw reads higher NDTI than any Cambe field, so most of it sits on the plateau.
A 9 ha quadrat is not a field: the norm samples quadrats inside each declared field.
Tillage between two clear observations can be missed; Landsat alone revisits every 16 days, and clouds leave gaps, so 'no bare-soil signature' is not proof of no tillage.
Wet soil hides the bare-soil signature (see the rain check in residue_landsat.json).
